extracted.intended_audience: state environmental agencies and plan developers implementing EPA emission guidelines under CAA section 111 (power sector state plans)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for designing and evaluating state plans under EPA emission guidelines for affected electric generating units (EGUs), including allowable compliance flexibilities (averaging, trading, unit-specific mass limits), how to demonstrate equivalence, and required safeguards (e.g., backstop rates).

rubrics_metrics.name: RULOF restrictions on compliance flexibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: RULOF provisions are intended for EGUs in unique circumstances and can yield less stringent standards of performance, longer compliance schedules, or alternate control technologies; EPA has concerns about how states will particularize compliance obligations using RULOF and about uncertainty in future utilization of RULOF-subject EGUs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA prohibits affected EGUs with a standard of performance based on RULOF from using unit-specific mass-based compliance because allowing RULOF sources to use unit-specific mass compliance could undermine state plan stringency (e.g., by enabling underperformance through averaging or trading with less stringent sources). RULOF should be used only where truly bespoke circumstances justify deviations; states should avoid designing mass-based compliance strategies that include RULOF sources due to compounding uncertainty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion of natural gas- and oil-fired steam subcategories from trading/averaging and unit-specific mass-based compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: The BSER determination for natural gas- and oil-fired steam subcategories does not require improvement in emission performance and offers flexibility for efficiency at different operating levels; these sources are unlikely to be responsive to incentives to overperform.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA prohibits including affected EGUs in the natural gas- and oil-fired steam subcategories in emission trading or averaging programs and from using unit-specific mass-based compliance because their participation could undermine equivalence (by incentivizing more-stringent sources to underperform) and add little overperformance value. States should exclude these subcategories from trading/averaging and unit-specific mass-based approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coal-fired subcategories eligible for compliance flexibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Both coal-fired subcategories (medium- and long-term) are allowed to participate in compliance flexibilities (averaging, trading, unit-specific mass compliance) within EPA parameters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA allows coal-fired EGUs to use these flexibilities but only under specific constraints described in the preamble (e.g., backstop rates for mass-based approaches, scope limits for averaging). States planning to include coal-fired sources should follow the EPA parameters and account for interactions with incentives like IRC section 45Q.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incentivizing overperformance and technology innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: Compliance flexibilities can incentivize affected EGUs to overperform relative to standards of performance, promoting innovation in control technologies and potentially lowering control costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA recognizes that overperformance is desirable and may be encouraged through trading/averaging and unit-specific mass compliance, and notes that EGUs benefiting from tax credits (e.g., IRC section 45Q) may still utilize operational flexibility. States should design flexibilities to reward overperformance while ensuring equivalence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inter-subcategory trading permitted for coal subcategories
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA is not finalizing a restriction on trading or averaging across the two coal-fired subcategories; medium-term coal-fired EGUs may trade or average with long-term coal-fired EGUs, subject to other restrictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States may permit trading/averaging between medium- and long-term coal subcategories provided all other EPA parameters and safeguards (e.g., backstop rates where applicable) are met and the program demonstrates equivalent stringency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope limitation of rate-based averaging
rubrics_metrics.description: Rate-based averaging may be implemented at the facility level (units within a single facility) or at the owner/operator level within a state, but not across owner/operators or at state or interstate levels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA limits averaging scope because broader averaging would require complex, near-real-time coordination of operating and emissions data across multiple utilities or states, reducing transparency and compliance-tracking ability. Where a state desires statewide or interstate rate-based flexibility, it must implement rate-based trading instead of averaging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggregate rate calculation for rate-based averaging (output-weighted)
rubrics_metrics.description: To ensure equivalence with unit-specific rate-based standards, the weighting of an aggregate compliance rate for averaging must be done on an output basis (gross generation-weighted average of each participating unit's required standard of performance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State plans must: specify the group of participating affected EGUs; state the unit-specific rate-based presumptive standard for each participating EGU; define the aggregate compliance rate and calculation method (gross generation-weighted average); and include self-executing provisions addressing changes in owner/operator during program implementation so no plan revision is required to maintain enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Only affected EGUs may participate in rate-based aggregate calculations
rubrics_metrics.description: Only affected EGUs are permitted to be included in the calculation of an aggregate rate-based standard of performance and in an aggregate compliance demonstration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States must not include non-affected sources in the averaging group or count reductions occurring at non-affected sources toward equivalence; plans must ensure the aggregate calculation includes only the regulated affected EGUs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Denomination of compliance instruments in rate-based trading (tons of CO2)
rubrics_metrics.description: In rate-based trading, the tradable compliance instrument must be denominated as one ton of CO2; instruments denominated in other units (e.g., MWh) are not fungible for this purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under EPA's method, compliance instruments are awarded at calendar year-end to EGUs performing below their standard at a quantity equal to (standard_rate - actual_rate) * gross_generation (MWh). Transfer and use of instruments are accounted for in the numerator (total annual CO2 emissions) of the CO2 emission rate when demonstrating compliance. States must require instruments denominated in tons CO2 to ensure fungibility and equivalence across participating EGUs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrating compliance in rate-based trading
rubrics_metrics.description: Each participating affected EGU demonstrates compliance based on its reported CO2 emission performance (lb CO2/MWh) and, if necessary, surrender of compliance instruments so that the demonstrated lb CO2/MWh is equivalent to or lower than the unit-specific rate-based standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States must specify participating EGUs and individual standards in the plan. Compliance is shown by combining reported performance with surrendered instruments (if needed). EPA requires the instrument be denominated in tons CO2 to preserve equivalence over time and avoid reliance on utilization assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preference for rate-based trading over averaging for wider scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a state wishes to implement rate-based compliance flexibilities across owner/operators or across states (statewide/interstate), EPA requires rate-based trading rather than averaging to ensure compliance and equivalent stringency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rate-based trading better accommodates broader geographic/organizational scope because it avoids the complex real-time coordination and transparency burdens associated with wide-scope averaging and inherently accounts for utilization via the rate calculation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unit-specific mass-based compliance requires a backstop emission rate
rubrics_metrics.description: If a state translates unit-specific rate-based standards into mass-based limits for unit-specific mass-based compliance, the mass limit must be accompanied by a backstop emission rate (expressed in lb CO2/MWh gross) for demonstrating compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA requires a backstop rate because CAA section 111 focuses on cleaner operation (rate-based metrics), and mass-based limits alone can be undermined by uncertain future utilization. The backstop ensures units operate more cleanly even if mass limits are non-binding due to lower-than-expected utilization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumptively approvable unit-specific mass approach for long-term coal-fired EGUs
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA finalizes a presumptively approvable unit-specific mass-based compliance approach for long-term coal-fired EGUs where the mass limit is set by multiplying the presumptively approvable rate by gross generation corresponding to an 80% annual capacity factor, and units must meet a backstop emission rate equivalent to an 80% reduction relative to baseline emission performance on an annual calendar-year basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States may adopt this presumptively approvable method; deviations are allowed but must still include a backstop rate and will be reviewed for reasonableness (e.g., if a state assumes utilization >80% the EPA will consider historical capacity factor data). EPA's confidence in this approach rests on the high stringency of the subcategory and incentives (e.g., 45Q tax credit) that encourage high capture/utilization.

rubrics_metrics.name: No presumptively approvable unit-specific mass approach for medium-term coal-fired EGUs; approval conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA is not finalizing a presumptively approvable mass-based compliance approach for medium-term coal-fired EGUs due to (1) uncertainty in future utilization and (2) relatively lower stringency (e.g., ~16% reduction), which can cause mass limits to be non-binding or ineffective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States may still propose unit-specific mass-based compliance for medium-term EGUs, but to be approvable the plan must (a) apply a backstop rate in conjunction with the mass limit (EPA suggests a possible illustrative backstop of ~14.5% reduction relative to baseline), and (b) demonstrate that the plan will achieve an equivalent level of emission reduction to unit-specific rate-based standards, including detailed documentation of how mass limits were calculated and justification for any utilization assumptions. EPA will apply high scrutiny to utilization assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mass-based emission trading requirements and safeguards
rubrics_metrics.description: Mass-based trading establishes an aggregate mass budget by converting unit-specific rate-based standards to mass limits using assumed utilization for each participating EGU, summing individual limits to an aggregate budget, and issuing tradable allowances (one allowance = one ton CO2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States must: specify how allowances will be distributed; require affected EGUs to surrender allowances equal to reported CO2 emissions each compliance period; ensure total emissions ≤ aggregate mass budget; and require each participating EGU to demonstrate compliance with the unit-specific backstop rate. EPA warns of heightened risk from compounding utilization uncertainty across multiple participating sources and requires backstop rates and other safeguards to maintain equivalence.

rubrics_metrics.name: States must demonstrate equivalence and may not rely on non-affected sources
rubrics_metrics.description: State plans must ensure an equivalent level of emission reduction to unit-specific rate-based standards for the affected EGUs; states cannot rely on emission reductions at non-affected sources to demonstrate equivalence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For any flexibility (averaging, trading, mass or rate-based), plans must include documentation and methods showing equivalence (e.g., participant lists, unit-specific standards, aggregate calculations, mass limit derivations, utilization assumptions). EPA will review such demonstrations for consistency with statute and emission guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and timely compliance data requirements for averaging/trading
rubrics_metrics.description: Limitations on the scope of averaging/trading are grounded in the need for transparency and timely availability of compliance-related information (operating and emissions data) to ensure aggregate compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA expects states to design programs at levels (facility or owner/operator within a state for averaging) where timely data sharing and transparency are practicable. Programs requiring coordination across many owners/operators or states would likely impede tracking and enforcement and therefore should use trading mechanisms or be otherwise structured to ensure timely data access.
